subject: Dedicated capacity guarantee questions and measurement agreement
messages:
From: Markus Weber <m.weber@brightpath.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity guarantee questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we move forward with a reserved commit we'd like to lock down a few specifics on what you can guarantee and how you measure it — the procurement team needs this for their internal sign-off.

Can you confirm:
- Guaranteed sustained throughput in tokens/sec for our Llama-2-based generation workload (typical request: 512 input tokens, 256 output tokens, batch size = 8)?
- Peak requests/sec envelope and how transient spikes are handled (burst vs throttling)?
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for 256-token generations and how those are measured.
- Measurement methodology: do you run customer-provided traces or synthetic load? How do you account for KV cache warmup and cold-starts?

Also, are there credit/discount mechanisms if the measured throughput underperforms the guarantee during the acceptance window?

We'll need this detail to finalize the term sheet. Attached is our procurement checklist (for your reference).

Best,
Markus
Head of Core Platform
BrightPath Analytics

Attachment: brightpath_procurement_checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Markus Weber <m.weber@brightpath.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantee questions

Hi Markus — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary of what Redwood can guarantee and the proposed measurement approach. I've attached a one-page SLA measurement plan and a redlineable term sheet for the commit.

Quick answers up front:
- Sustained throughput guarantee: 4.5M tokens/sec aggregate for a 64-GPU pool (quantized model variant as discussed) measured after a 30-minute warmup window. We express guarantees as aggregate tokens/sec per committed GPU pool band.
- Spike handling: burst capacity available up to 1.5x for short windows (≤5 minutes) subject to overall pool utilization; beyond that we route to compatible model variant or throttle according to the configured fallback policy.
- Latency SLOs: for 256-token generation on the quantized variant with batching similar to your profile — p50 ≤ 120ms, p95 ≤ 400ms, p99 ≤ 900ms. SLOs assume steady-state with warm KV cache.

Measurement methodology (high level):
1) Acceptance window: a 72-hour measurement window scheduled during mutually agreed days.
2) We run two parallel runs: (a) Redwood synthetic runner (replay engine) using your trace to validate tooling and (b) BrightPath's trace replay (customer-provided) executed on the dedicated pool.
3) Warmup: first 30 minutes excluded from agreement measurement to allow for KV cache and batching steady-state.
4) Metrics: tokens/sec (aggregate), requests/sec, per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), model error rate (if you provide reference outputs), and success rate (no timeouts/errors).
5) Pass criteria: aggregate tokens/sec >= guaranteed band for ≥95% of 10-minute windows over the 72-hour acceptance window; latency SLOs must meet configured thresholds for ≥95% of requests.

Credits/Remedy: If we miss guarantees, we provide proportionate credit against committed fees for the affected month(s) and offer a remediation run at no extra cost. Exact credit formula included in attached term sheet.

Next steps: Rishi and Soojin — can we schedule a measurement kickoff for next week? Markus, if the summary looks right I'll send the redlined term sheet.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_measurement-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), commit_term_sheet_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Markus Weber <m.weber@brightpath.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantee questions

Laura / Soojin — quick internal notes and asks for the kickoff:

- Soojin: confirm the exact command-line flags and replay tooling we will provide BrightPath. They need a way to replay their traces deterministically. Also list default batch scheduling config that maps to the 4.5M tokens/sec figure.
- Legal/pricing: recommend we offer a limited 10% up-front discount for an annual commit if they sign within two weeks; escalate larger discounts to me.
- Measurement topology: propose we run the Redwood runner first to sanity-check the pool and then run customer trace. That order reduces noisy failures.

Markus — if you approve the order above, I'll lock the dates. We should also confirm preferred time zone for the 72-hour window (we recommend US-PST overnight start to reduce daytime spikes).

Rishi
Head of Sales, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Weber <m.weber@brightpath.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guarantee questions

Laura — this looks good and addresses most of our concerns. A couple of quick clarifications before we move to signature:

- Can you add an explicit clause that performance credits are pro-rated by the percentage shortfall in aggregate tokens/sec during the measurement window? Procurement needs that spelled out.
- For the warmup exclusion, can we shorten to 15 minutes if we jointly run a pre-warm phase? That would help us in time-constrained launch cycles.

On the discount: the procurement team will push for an additional 5% if we can get a 90-day rollback clause in the first quarter. Happy to discuss with Rishi.

If you can add the pro-rata credit language and the optional pre-warm clause to the term sheet I'll loop in our legal and we can get to signature.

Thanks,
Markus
